items.markingKey: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64; 12 is 4 × 3. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why 5⁻² = 1/25 by continuing the pattern 5², 5¹, 5⁰.
items.answer: 5² = 25, 5¹ = 5, 5⁰ = 1: each step down divides by 5, so 5⁻¹ = 1/5 and 5⁻² = 1/25.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: 5² = 25, 5¹ = 5, 5⁰ = 1: each step down divides by 5, so 5⁻¹ = 1/5 and 5⁻² = 1/25. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Without converting to ordinary numbers, explain which is larger: 6.5 × 10⁶ or 1.5 × 10⁷.
items.answer: 1.5 × 10⁷ is larger: it has the higher power of 10, and both front numbers lie between 1 and 10.
items.markingKey: Compare exponents first (R1); a higher power of 10 always wins when both are in standard form (R1).

items.stem: "(2x)³ = 2x³" Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Every factor in the bracket is cubed: (2x)³ = 8x³.
items.markingKey: Every factor in the bracket is cubed: (2x)³ = 8x³. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Without a calculator, find the two consecutive integers between which ∛126 lies, and state which one it is closer to.
items.markingKey: 5³ = 125 < 126 < 216 = 6³ (M1 A1); compare distances 1 and 90 (R1).

items.markingKey: Divide the numbers and subtract the exponents (M1); adjust so 1 ≤ a < 10 (M1); 8.88 × 10⁻⁵ (A1).

items.stem: Lars sends a message to 2 friends, and each of them forwards it to 2 new friends, and so on. (a) Show that 2⁶ people receive it in round 6. (b) Find the total number of people who have received it after 6 rounds. (c) Explain why the pattern cannot continue for long in a city of 2 million people.
items.answer: (a) each round multiplies by 2, so round n gives 2ⁿ (b) 126 (c) 2ⁿ grows so fast that it passes 2 000 000 by round 21
items.markingKey: (a) each round multiplies by 2, so round n gives 2ⁿ (b) 126 (c) 2ⁿ grows so fast that it passes 2 000 000 by round 21. Pattern identified and written with exponents (B: M1 A1); evaluated correctly (A1); reasoning/limit explained (R1 C1).

items.stem: A cube-shaped water tank holds 512 m³. (a) Find the length of its edge. (b) Find the area of the base. (c) How deep is the water when the tank holds 448 m³?
items.markingKey: (a) 8 m (b) 64 m² (c) 7 m. Correct inverse operation (root) used (M1 A1); further calculation (M1 A1); units and reasoning communicated (C1).

items.stem: Investigate the values of 6ⁿ for n = 2, 1, 0, −1, −2. (a) Show your results in a table. (b) Describe what happens to the value as n decreases. (c) Is 6ⁿ ever zero or negative? Justify your answer.
items.answer: (a) 36, 6, 1, 1/6, 1/36 (b) it is divided by 6 each time and approaches 0 (c) no – each value is a positive number divided by 6, which stays positive

items.stem: A region around Lisbon has a population of 7.8 × 10⁷ people and an area of 8.5 × 10⁵ km². (a) Calculate the population density in people per km², giving your answer in standard form to 3 s.f. (b) Explain whether the answer is reasonable.
items.answer: (a) 9.18 × 10¹ people per km² (b) it is about 92 people per km², sensible compared with real cities and countryside
